REGENT OF BELITUNG

DECIDES:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE.

heading: CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Belitung Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Belitung.
4. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus of Belitung Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of Belitung Regency.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
7. Woman….

D:\PERDA PDF\2-PERDA PERLINDUNGAN HAK PEREMPUAN DAN ANAK.doc 3

7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and/or for and on behalf of another party who is their dependent.
10. Protection is all prevention, service and empowerment actions to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
13. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to engage in business/enterprise and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
14. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Accompaniment is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and children.
16. Counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert/trained person in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim and/or perpetrator increases in solving the problems faced.
17. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
18. Forum….

D:\PERDA PDF\2-PERDA PERLINDUNGAN HAK PEREMPUAN DAN ANAK.doc 4

18. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for the prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is established at the regency, sub-district and village/kelurahan levels.
19. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children.
21. Household is family members and relatives including grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and non-relatives including maids and drivers who live and eat from 1 (one) kitchen and reside in 1 (one) house.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 8

Obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. regional government;
b. society;
c. family; and
d. parents.

heading: Article 9

4. Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

1. The obligations and responsibilities of society as referred to in Article 8 letter b, shall be conducted in the form of community participation.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.
(3) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 8 letters c and d include having full legal responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect women and children as family members.

heading: Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

Every person who hears, sees, or knows of the occurrence of violence against women and children shall make efforts in accordance with their capacity to:
a. prevent and stop the continuation of acts of violence;
b. provide protection to victims;
d. provide….

e. assist in the process of filing an application for protection order.

Article 21

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 22

1. In order to provide protection services to women and children from violence, the Regional Government shall establish PPT as an integrated service center for the protection of women and children from violence including victims of violence.
2. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), functions as an integrated service center in providing protection to women and children from violence.
3. Further provisions regarding the Organization and Working Procedures of PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 23
Article 24
Article 25
Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. The task force for the protection of women and children at the sub-district level as referred to in Article 23 letter c, is a functional work unit that provides integrated protection services and handling of cases of violence against women and children at the sub-district level.
2. The membership of the task force for the protection of women and children at the sub-district level as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of sub-district apparatus elements, district/agency elements at the sub-district level, police sector (Polsek) elements, military rayon command (Koramil) elements, community/religious leaders, and youth elements.
3. Further provisions regarding the establishment, duties and functions of the task force as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by Sub-district Head Decree.

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

1. The domestic violence prevention group at the urban village/village level as referred to in Article 23 letter d, is a functional work unit that provides integrated protection services and handling of cases of violence against women and children at the urban village/village level.
2. The domestic violence prevention group at the urban village/village level as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of urban village/village apparatus elements, babinsa and babinkamtibmas elements, community/religious leaders, and youth elements.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, duties and functions of the task force as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by urban village head/village head decree.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

Part One

Cooperation

heading: Article 28
Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of acts of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of acts of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who are withdrawn/neglected from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
3. The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

REPORTING

Article 30

1. PPT is obligated to report the implementation of the provision of protection for women and children from acts of violence to the Regent.
2. The reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. services; and
c. performance.
3. The submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

heading: CHAPTER XIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 31

1. The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the provision of protection for women and children from acts of violence.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Guidance….

Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2), is in order to realize the objectives of protecting the rights of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by relevant OPD/agencies and the community.

heading: Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

1. The Regional Government is obligated to conduct supervision of the provision of protection for the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
2. The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be conducted with professional, transparent, and accountable principles.

heading: Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

The community may conduct supervision of the provision of protection for women and children from acts of violence organized by the Regional Government through a mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Regent and/or DPRD.

heading: ELUCIDATION
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BELITUNG REGENCY

NUMBER 2 YEAR 2018

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF THE RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their position as vulnerable to becoming victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both inside and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Government of Belitung Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 Year 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 Year 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Belitung Regency has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so forth.

Therefore....

Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of the Rights of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of the Rights of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government and the participation of the business sector and community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be eliminated. Through this Regional Regulation it is expected to better implement the rights of children and women and their protection, so that it can be implemented more comprehensively, integrated and continuously by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to child and women protection efforts.

heading: Article 3
translated_text:
Article 3

Point a The principle of humanity becomes the foundation of the concept of protection of women and children from acts of violence, which is respect for human rights and the dignity of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).

Point b The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role....

D:\PERDA PDF\2-PERDA PERLINDUNGAN HAK PEREMPUAN DAN ANAK.doc 22 play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Point c The principle of non-discrimination that in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence does not discriminate on the basis of age, gender, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Point d Principle of Victim Protection The principle of protection is a principle that functions to provide protection to women and children in order to provide peace in family and community life.

Point e Principle of Empowerment The principle of best interests for women and children, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities and Regional Governments to fulfill the rights of women and children as regulated in laws and regulations.

Point f Principle of Integration

heading: Article 4
translated_text:
Article 4

Point a What is meant by trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification of documents or identity, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control or the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

Point… D:\PERDA PDF\2-PERDA PERLINDUNGAN HAK PEREMPUAN DAN ANAK.doc 23 Point b What is meant by exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical sexual reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring/utilizing labor or transplanting organs and or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits.

Point c Sufficiently clear.

Point d Sufficiently clear.

Point e What is meant by witness is a person who sees, hears and experiences events of violence and human rights violations.

Point f Mediation is carried out for cases of domestic violence that fall into the category of complaint offenses as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence.

heading: Article 5
translated_text:
Article 5

Point a Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Point b Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Point c Sexual violence is caused by:

1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. coercion....

D:\PERDA PDF\2-PERDA PERLINDUNGAN HAK PEREMPUAN DAN ANAK.doc 24

2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point d Neglect is caused by:

1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of a child as appropriate, carried out by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they must provide life, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Point e Coercion/Deprivation of Freedom is a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will and restricts their freedom as a human being who has the right to determine choices.

Point f Exploitation is caused by:

1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
2. acts….

D:\PERDA PDF\2-PERDA PERLINDUNGAN HAK PEREMPUAN DAN ANAK.doc 25

2. acts with or without the consent of the victim including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Point g Threat of certain actions is a form of intimidation to do or not do what is requested by the perpetrator with consequences that are not good for the victim.

Point h Other violence is caused among others by any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear.

Point g What is meant by the victim's right to rehabilitation includes access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance for the restoration of civil rights, restoration of good name, citizenship.

What is meant by assistance is individuals who work as volunteers to provide protection and support to women and children who are victims of violence during the judicial process, these assistants can come from family members, friends and independent organizations that pay attention to witnesses and victims or advocates.
